title: Match on resolved module identity, not specifier strings
note: Both T93 bypasses closed. Relative import (../../../lib/prisma) and barrel re-export now block; the clean control still passes; external suite 7/7 with ZERO baseline drift, so no overshoot.
evidence: The plan premise was partly wrong and the real defect was in a different place. Tracing it: (1) the engine graph matcher was never even called during a check - no debug output at all; (2) the deciding logic is a CLI-side PRE-FILTER, graphImportResolvesToForbidden, which had the identical defect - isForbiddenImport(resolvedPath, forbiddenImports) compares a resolved file path against specifiers; (3) even after fixing that, the engine receives a graph SCOPED TO THE CHANGED FILES, so it cannot derive what @/lib/prisma means - the imports establishing that live outside the diff; (4) MODULE_REEXPORTS_MODULE was not in the kept-edge list, so the barrel chain never reached the engine.
diagnosis: Fix is in four parts: CLI computes forbidden module identities from the FULL graph before scoping; passes them to the engine as matcher.forbidden_module_files; the engine prefers supplied identities and still derives locally for whole-repo checks; and re-export edges are kept in the scoped graph. Also found and recorded a fixture defect: my own T93 fixtures did not reproduce the bypass - inference learned the relative specifier in one and inferred nothing in the other. The scenario only reproduces when the contract learns the alias form from legitimate usage first, and it needs a tsconfig paths mapping, without which the resolver produces 1 resolved edge out of 64 imports.

title: Rebuild the T93 fixtures so they actually reproduce
note: The fixtures I committed in run 1 did not reproduce the bypass they were filed for. Each now carries a tsconfig paths mapping and a route violating via the ALIAS form, so inference learns @/lib/prisma and the sneaky route is genuinely the odd one out. Pinned by packages/cli/test/bypass-fixtures.test.ts, which drives the real CLI end to end.
evidence: Before the rebuild: bypass-relative-import inferred forbidden_imports=[../../../lib/prisma] - it learned the sneaky form, so the route matched trivially by string and the fixture would have passed even with the bug present. bypass-barrel-reexport inferred nothing at all (forbidden_imports: None), so there was no contract to enforce. Both now detect the sneaky route, and both would fail if T100 were reverted.
diagnosis: A fixture that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no fixture - it converts an open bug into apparent coverage. Also recorded in the test: without tsconfig paths the resolver produces one resolved edge out of sixty-four imports, so resolved-identity matching has nothing to work with.

title: T01c: block-mode contract, finding reports enforcement none
note: REPRODUCED deterministically, and the scope is four times larger than T01c stated. Root cause narrowed to one gate; not yet fixed.
evidence: Two corrections to run 1 framing. (1) It is NOT midday-only: the baseline shows enforcement_matches_mode False on FOUR repos - taxonomy (warn->none), calcom (block->none), papermark (warn->none), midday (block->none) - and correct on only three (dub warn, formbricks block, openstatus block). Run 1 recorded it as the single mismatch across seven repos, which was wrong. (2) It is NOT the --data-modules path: midday injection blocks correctly by hand (enforcement=block, blocking=1) with the declared contract, and the declared convention materialises correctly (kind=api_route_no_direct_data_access, mode=block, capability=deterministic_check).
diagnosis: The trigger is route COUNT, not the declared path. Bisected on midday: bad route alone -> block. bad+clean -> none. bad+lookalike -> none. bad+subpath -> none. bad+typeonly -> block (the only one that does not trigger, because T12 drops the type-only import so that route contributes no import fact). So ANY second route with a real import collapses enforcement_result to none. Strong candidate mechanism: check_command.rs:280 downgrades enforcement_result to "none" whenever can_block is false, and can_block (line 37) is completeness_reasons.is_empty(), fed by check_graph_completeness_reasons which flags unresolved_import on API route files. NOT CONFIRMED: the CLI-reported capability_completeness.can_block stays True with no unresolved diagnostics surfaced, so the engine internal gate is computed from something in the scoped request that the CLI payload does not expose. Next step is to instrument completeness_reasons directly in the engine for the two-route case.

title: A6 discovery: workspace-package resolution and message suppression
diagnosis: Both halves were already fixed; the plan premise (from run-1 discoveries T01a/T01b) is stale. specifierPointsAt already resolves workspace package names through workspaceDirs built from the workspace manifest, and start.ts line 224 already appends the discovery text when a candidate exists. Verified empirically on midday, which has 3 convention candidates: the message IS visible, names packages/supabase/src/client/server.ts with the local path, states it is imported by 2 routes as @midday/supabase/server, explains that inference only recognises prisma/database/db names, and gives the exact --data-modules command. That is the DoD, met.
evidence: The harness already asserts the discovery half via f4_gap_exercised (inference_alone_found_data_layer false AND discovery_named_data_layer true), which is why midday shows f4gap=y. What was NOT guarded was the text-output visibility, so added packages/cli/test/discovery-message.test.ts - 3 tests covering the wrapper-named case, the declared-dependencies-only case, and the no-discovery fallback. Suppressing that message would restore exactly the blindness that made F4 invisible.

title: Intermittent MCP parity flake at default concurrency
evidence: pnpm -r test failed once on mcp.test.ts "proves cross-surface canonical route parity for CLI and MCP route contracts" (1 failed / 56 passed), then passed in isolation (53/53) and on two consecutive full workspace runs.
diagnosis: T64 removed --workspace-concurrency=1 on the strength of four consecutive green runs and a confirmed root cause (SQLITE_BUSY, fixed by T17 busy_timeout). This is a fifth-run failure, so either the busy_timeout window is occasionally too short under load or there is a second contention source. Recording rather than dismissing: T64 explicitly warns against reaching for serialisation before establishing the cause, and one flake is not yet a cause.

title: T01c: block-mode contract, finding reports enforcement none
note: RESOLVED, and the product behaviour was correct all along. enforcement_matches_mode is now true on all seven repos and promoted to a HARD ASSERTION - verified to bite by forcing it false, which flips midday to FAIL.
evidence: Traced the full chain with a file-based probe in the engine (CLI swallows engine stderr). bad route alone -> can_block=true, reasons=[], enforcement=block. bad+clean -> can_block=false, reasons=[unresolved_route_import_symbol:.../drift-eval-clean/route.ts]. check_command.rs:280 then downgrades EVERY finding to none. Two causes, both in the harness: (1) midday cleanSymbol was "sanitizeRedirect" but the module exports sanitizeRedirectPath - importing a symbol that does not exist; (2) structurally, the lookalike and subpath negative controls MUST import non-existent modules, and an unresolvable import on any route in scope legitimately makes coverage incomplete. So the harness suppressed the very thing it was measuring.
diagnosis: Run 1 called this an F3-class silent failure in the product. It is not - Drift declining to block when it cannot resolve an import on a route in the checked scope is the completeness contract working as designed, and packages/engine-contract enforces it as a schema refinement (blocking findings require complete capability coverage). I first implemented per-file gating in the engine and reverted it: it produces results the contract rejects, and the invariant is deliberate and tested. Fix is in the harness - measure enforcement in an isolated check containing only the injected violation. Also corrected run 1 scope claim: FOUR repos were affected (taxonomy, calcom, papermark, midday), not one.

title: Gitignore correctness via per-directory semantics
note: Adopted ignore::WalkBuilder for file discovery. Nested .gitignore files and ! negations now work, patterns stay scoped to the directory that declares them, and the external suite is 7/7 with zero drift - openstatus keeps injection_caught and catches_genuine_subpath, the exact fields the first attempt regressed.
evidence: Fixture test/fixtures/gitignore-nested carries the shape that reverted attempt 1: a bare `app` pattern in packages/server/.gitignore plus API routes in packages/dashboard. Four assertions - root ignore applies, nested ignore applies, ! negation re-includes, and the bare pattern stays local. Deliberately narrow about ignore sources (gitignore and git exclude only, no global or per-user files, nothing above the repo root) so two machines scanning the same commit see the same files.
diagnosis: Caught a regression I introduced, and the distinction matters: the hand-rolled walk got root failure for free via fs::read_dir(repo_root)?, while WalkBuilder yields it as an error entry. Treating that like any other unreadable path made a scan of a NON-EXISTENT repo report an empty repo and exit 0 - success for a repository it never saw. Now the root must be readable or the scan fails, while per-entry errors deeper in the tree stay diagnostics, because partial coverage that says so is honest and one unreadable subdirectory should not lose a scan. Found by an existing test (persists failed scan manifests), not by inspection.
